Step 2 - Homographies from view 1 to views 2, 3, 4 (DLT)

With 8 points, $A$ is 16 × 9. Its smallest singular value $\sigma_9$ would be exactly 0 for noise-free clicks. $\hat{\mathbf h}$ is the matching right singular vector, then un-normalised and scaled so that $\sigma_2(H) = 1$, with the sign chosen for positive depth.

View 1 → view 2

$$ \sigma_8(A) = 1.492,\quad \sigma_9(A) = 0.08616 \qquad H_{2} = \begin{bmatrix}0.1292 & 0.8209 & 0.0226 \\ -2.1430 & 0.0139 & -0.1466 \\ 1.1872 & -0.1150 & 1.2653\end{bmatrix},\qquad K H K^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix}0.7633 & 0.7572 & -299.5205 \\ -1.2693 & -0.0711 & 1684.1362 \\ 0.0011 & -0.0001 & 0.7161\end{bmatrix} $$

Transfer error (view-1 clicks mapped by the pixel homography vs. the clicks in view 2): 20.87 px on average. Eigenvalues of $H^{\mathsf T}H$: 6.6757, 1.0000, 0.6532 (the middle one is 1 by construction).

View 1 → view 3

$$ \sigma_8(A) = 1.646,\quad \sigma_9(A) = 0.0363 \qquad H_{3} = \begin{bmatrix}0.1009 & 0.9339 & 0.0079 \\ -2.0819 & 0.0118 & -0.3685 \\ 1.3499 & -0.2158 & 1.3469\end{bmatrix},\qquad K H K^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix}0.8219 & 0.8162 & -350.6319 \\ -1.0874 & -0.1477 & 1460.1406 \\ 0.0012 & -0.0002 & 0.7854\end{bmatrix} $$

Transfer error (view-1 clicks mapped by the pixel homography vs. the clicks in view 3): 7.07 px on average. Eigenvalues of $H^{\mathsf T}H$: 7.4113, 1.0000, 0.6244 (the middle one is 1 by construction).

$$ \sigma_8(A) = 1.432,\quad \sigma_9(A) = 0.05943 \qquad H_{4} = \begin{bmatrix}0.0597 & 1.0178 & 0.2170 \\ -0.8800 & -0.0094 & -0.3622 \\ 0.7136 & 0.0576 & 0.9049\end{bmatrix},\qquad K H K^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix}0.4409 & 1.0454 & -343.3079 \\ -0.3536 & 0.0332 & 522.2489 \\ 0.0006 & 5.19e-05 & 0.4812\end{bmatrix} $$

Transfer error (view-1 clicks mapped by the pixel homography vs. the clicks in view 4): 10.74 px on average. Eigenvalues of $H^{\mathsf T}H$: 2.1914, 1.0000, 0.1324 (the middle one is 1 by construction).

Step 3 - Decomposing $H = R + \mathbf T\mathbf N^{\mathsf T}$

Each homography gives four candidate $(R, \mathbf T, \mathbf N)$. Positive depth needs $\mathbf N^{\mathsf T}\mathbf m_1 > 0$ for all 8 points. Among the survivors, we pick the combination whose three normals agree best.

Step 4 - Camera matrices

With $d = 1$ (plane-distance units), the normalised camera matrices from step 3 are:

$$ [R_{1} \mid \mathbf T_{1}] = \begin{bmatrix}1.0000 & 0.0000 & 0.0000 & 0.0000 \\ 0.0000 & 1.0000 & 0.0000 & 0.0000 \\ 0.0000 & 0.0000 & 1.0000 & 0.0000\end{bmatrix} $$ $$ [R_{2} \mid \mathbf T_{2}] = \begin{bmatrix}0.4257 & 0.8914 & 0.1554 & -0.3325 \\ -0.8387 & 0.3242 & 0.4376 & -1.4625 \\ 0.3397 & -0.3166 & 0.8856 & 0.9503\end{bmatrix} $$ $$ [R_{3} \mid \mathbf T_{3}] = \begin{bmatrix}0.2785 & 0.9498 & 0.1426 & -0.2235 \\ -0.7653 & 0.1297 & 0.6305 & -1.6569 \\ 0.5803 & -0.2847 & 0.7630 & 0.9685\end{bmatrix} $$ $$ [R_{4} \mid \mathbf T_{4}] = \begin{bmatrix}0.0165 & 0.9969 & -0.0773 & 0.2982 \\ -0.7263 & 0.0651 & 0.6843 & -1.0604 \\ 0.6872 & 0.0448 & 0.7251 & 0.1822\end{bmatrix} $$

Step 5 - Triangulating point 1

Two rows per view, $x\,\mathbf p^{3\mathsf T} - \mathbf p^{1\mathsf T}$ and $y\,\mathbf p^{3\mathsf T} - \mathbf p^{2\mathsf T}$, stacked into an 8 × 4 matrix:

$$ A = \begin{bmatrix}-1.0000 & 0.0000 & 0.2907 & 0.0000 \\ -0.0000 & -1.0000 & -0.4778 & -0.0000 \\ -0.4964 & -0.8255 & -0.3398 & 0.1346 \\ 0.6749 & -0.1715 & -0.8647 & 1.0042 \\ -0.4106 & -0.8850 & -0.3164 & 0.0029 \\ 0.4563 & 0.0219 & -1.0367 & 1.1412 \\ -0.1817 & -1.0076 & -0.0970 & -0.3420 \\ 0.3420 & -0.0901 & -1.0898 & 0.9585\end{bmatrix} $$ $$ \sigma(A) = (2.73716,\ 2.03267,\ 0.99774,\ 0.19951) \;\Rightarrow\; \tilde{\mathbf X} = \begin{bmatrix}-0.16699 \\ 0.31967 \\ -0.71820 \\ -0.59508\end{bmatrix} \;\Rightarrow\; \mathbf X_1 = \tilde{\mathbf X}_{1:3}/\tilde X_4 = \begin{bmatrix}0.2806 \\ -0.5372 \\ 1.2069\end{bmatrix} $$

Check with the plane: $\mathbf N^{\mathsf T}\mathbf X_1 = 0.9992$ (should be $d = 1$), and the one-view shortcut $\mathbf m_1/(\mathbf N^{\mathsf T}\mathbf m_1) = (0.3369, -0.5537, 1.1591)$.

Projecting $\mathbf X_1$ back into every view, $\tilde{\mathbf x} = K(R\mathbf X_1 + \mathbf T)$ and then dividing by the third coordinate:

Step 7 - Scale, plane and boundary

$$ s = \frac{L}{\lVert \mathbf X_{1} - \mathbf X_{2} \rVert} = \frac{10.00\ \text{cm}}{20170854.84182} = 0.000\ \text{cm per unit} $$
